articles.title: People who favor dark humor tend to exhibit more problematic personality traits
articles.summary: The way a person jokes may offer a glimpse into their psychological makeup. A recent study suggests that people who favor darker humor, such as sarcasm and cynicism, tend to show higher levels of maladaptive personality traits.

articles.title: Weight-loss drugs linked to rare eye condition in massive data review
articles.summary: A comprehensive analysis of nearly 1.6 million patients suggests that popular diabetes and obesity medications may increase the risk of a rare condition that causes sudden vision loss, though the absolute risk remains very low.

articles.title: The “sense of absence” may explain why disconnected teens turn to addictive behaviors
articles.summary: New research suggests adolescents who feel emotionally unnoticed are more likely to engage in addictive behaviors. A newly developed psychological scale reveals how this “sense of absence” acts as a bridge connecting family struggles to teen addiction.

articles.title: Global data shows a sharp rise in adult ADHD diagnoses and medication prescriptions
articles.summary: ADHD diagnoses and medication prescriptions are surging globally, particularly among adults and women. This trend reflects improved clinical recognition of historically overlooked demographics, fundamentally shifting the understanding of the neurodevelopmental condition across the human lifespan.

articles.title: Schizophrenia’s lost brain connections follow a surprising pattern
articles.summary: Specialized brain scans reveal that schizophrenia is linked to widespread loss of the synapses that connect brain cells, with the left side of the brain hit especially hard. The damage follows a surprisingly organized pattern tied to the brain’s chemistry and wiring. Researchers also identified a left frontal region that may serve as a starting point for the loss.

articles.title: Ozempic does something unexpected to the brain’s hunger neurons
articles.summary: Ozempic may work in the brain in almost the opposite way scientists expected, activating hunger-linked neurons that appear essential for sustaining fat loss. The surprising discovery in mice could reveal new targets for developing even more effective obesity drugs.

articles.title: Oxytocin has opposite effects on men’s generosity depending on a their childhood experiences
articles.summary: Childhood adversity might alter how the brain responds to social hormones. A study in Translational Psychiatry suggests oxytocin temporarily increases altruism in adults with difficult childhoods, but decreases generosity in those with fewer adverse early experiences.

articles.title: Researchers reveal deeper workings of brain’s information hub
articles.summary: The brain has a remarkably flexible system for handling uncertainty and changing situations. Researchers found that the frontoparietal cortex constantly shifts how it communicates with other brain regions depending on what information is needed to make a decision. Rather than simply becoming more active when things get difficult, this network appears to reorganize itself in real time.

articles.summary: Women experiencing physical symptoms of stress, like headaches or muscle pain, report more negative dreams. A new psychological survey explores how daytime physical discomfort and general bodily awareness relate to the emotional intensity of our nighttime narratives.

articles.title: Holtercare-Bench: A Multimodal Benchmark for Evaluating Long-Term Dynamic ECG Analysis
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.19297v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While multimodal large language models (MLLMs) excel in medical applications, most of them favor static images or short-term signals. In the critical field of dynamic electrocardiograms (ECG), models struggle with complex temporal reasoning and diagnostic report generation due to a lack of high-quality datasets and benchmarks. To address this, we introduce (i) Holtercare-23K, a large-scale multimodal dynamic ECG dataset comprising 22,980 QA pairs derived from 788 clinical Holter records and featuring a novel signal-video-text tri-modal alignment.
